title: SDK session survives rejected logout and direct API access is restricted
full_title: SDK session survives rejected logout and direct API access is restricted
proposed_title: untrusted mutations are rejected without destroying the signed-in session
behavior: Rejected logout preserves identity; disallowed direct API path and cross-origin server mutation are blocked.
retained_assertions: User 200 and subject, logout403, nosniff header, subsequent authenticated user200, direct API404, server mutation403.
removed_assertions: SDK branding and a compound title that hides independent boundary scenarios; simultaneous invalid origin and invalid CSRF as proof of either independent guard.
replacement: Split into named behavioral cases: rejected cross-origin logout preserves same subject; same-origin logout with invalid CSRF preserves session; trusted logout control succeeds and ends session; direct /api/v1/inquiries is unavailable without backend forwarding; cross-origin POST to an actual mutation URL captured from a legitimate isolated form interaction is rejected and causes no additional backend mutation. Remove the unknown-path-only assertion once actual mutation rejection and successful controls pass; no independent nonexistent-endpoint contract is proposed. Use same-origin valid-CSRF controls to avoid a rejects-everything implementation passing. Scope backend observations per authenticated session or exclusive guest fixture.
coverage_risk: Preserve security header, identity survival, private API restriction, and origin rejection; tests must distinguish guards.
rationale: This is real HTTP boundary behavior, not a source/migration guard. Current compound case masks which guard rejects, and unknown mutation path cannot demonstrate a real mutation would be blocked.
verification: Disable origin validation and independently CSRF validation; each relevant negative case must fail. Make logout always reject; successful control must fail. Expose direct API forwarding; no-forwarding/404 case must fail, restore and pass.
